questions.prompt: A bag contains 5 red marbles, 7 blue marbles, and 8 green marbles. If one marble is chosen at random, what is the probability that it is NOT blue?
questions.explanation: There are $5 + 8 = 13$ non-blue marbles out of 20.

questions.prompt: A spinner is divided into 8 equal sections, and 3 of the sections are red. What is the probability that the spinner lands on a red section?
questions.explanation: 3 favorable sections out of 8.

questions.prompt: The table shows how many students in two grades play a school sport. If a student who does not play a sport is chosen at random, what is the probability that the student is in grade 11?
questions.explanation: Only students who do not play count: $55 + 40 = 95$. Of these, 40 are in grade 11, and $\dfrac{40}{95} = \dfrac{8}{19}$.

questions.prompt: The table summarizes a survey of 200 visitors to a planetarium. If one of the visitors who had visited before is selected at random, what is the probability that this visitor is under 18?
questions.explanation: Only the 60 visitors who had visited before count, and 24 of them are under 18: $\dfrac{24}{60} = \dfrac{2}{5}$. The value $\dfrac{3}{10}$ is $\dfrac{24}{80}$, which uses the wrong group.

questions.prompt: A box contains 40 ceramic tiles: 14 are blue, 16 are white, and 10 are green. If one tile is chosen at random, what is the probability that it is green?
questions.explanation: 10 of the $14 + 16 + 10 = 40$ tiles are green: $\dfrac{10}{40} = \dfrac{1}{4}$.

questions.prompt: At an astronomy camp, each of 160 campers chose exactly one workshop: 90 chose telescopes and 70 chose rockets. Of the campers who chose telescopes, $\dfrac{2}{3}$ were first-time campers, and of those who chose rockets, $\dfrac{3}{7}$ were first-time campers. If a first-time camper is selected at random, what is the probability that this camper chose rockets?
questions.explanation: There are $\dfrac{2}{3}(90) = 60$ first-time telescope campers and $\dfrac{3}{7}(70) = 30$ first-time rocket campers, so the probability is $\dfrac{30}{60 + 30} = \dfrac{1}{3}$.

questions.prompt: The table shows the results of a survey in which 160 students said whether they prefer print books or e-books. If a grade 9 student from the survey is chosen at random, what is the probability that the student prefers e-books?
questions.explanation: Only the 80 grade 9 students count, and 42 of them prefer e-books: $\dfrac{42}{80} = \dfrac{21}{40}$.

questions.prompt: In a class of 30 students, 18 students take Spanish, 12 take French, and 5 take both. If a student from the class is chosen at random, what is the probability that the student takes French but not Spanish?
questions.explanation: Of the 12 French students, 5 also take Spanish, so $12 - 5 = 7$ take French but not Spanish. The probability is $\dfrac{7}{30}$. Using 12 instead of 7 gives $\dfrac{2}{5}$.

questions.prompt: A jar contains 4 green marbles and 6 yellow marbles. Two marbles are drawn at random, one after the other, without replacement. What is the probability that both marbles are green?
questions.explanation: The first marble is green with probability $\dfrac{4}{10}$. After one green marble is removed, 3 of the remaining 9 are green, so the probability is $\dfrac{4}{10} \cdot \dfrac{3}{9} = \dfrac{12}{90} = \dfrac{2}{15}$. The value $\dfrac{4}{25}$ assumes the first marble is put back.

questions.prompt: A seed company tested 300 seeds of two varieties, Red and Gold. The table shows the results. If one of the seeds that germinated is selected at random, what is the probability that it is a Gold seed?
questions.explanation: Only the 240 seeds that germinated count. Of these, 114 are Gold: $\dfrac{114}{240} = \dfrac{19}{40}$. Dividing by the 150 Gold seeds instead gives $\dfrac{19}{25}$, which answers a different question.

questions.prompt: Of the 30 students in a class, 18 have visited Paris. If one student from the class is chosen at random, what is the probability that the student has NOT visited Paris?
questions.explanation: $30 - 18 = 12$ students have not visited, so the probability is $\dfrac{12}{30} = \dfrac{2}{5}$. $\dfrac{3}{5}$ is the probability that the student *has* visited.

questions.prompt: A bag contains only red tiles and blue tiles. If one tile is drawn at random, the probability that it is red is $\dfrac{3}{8}$. After 10 more red tiles are added to the bag, the probability of drawing a red tile is $\dfrac{1}{2}$. How many tiles were in the bag before the red tiles were added?
questions.explanation: With $n$ tiles at first, there are $\dfrac{3n}{8}$ red ones. Then $\dfrac{3n/8 + 10}{n + 10} = \dfrac{1}{2}$, so $\dfrac{3n}{4} + 20 = n + 10$ and $n = 40$. 15 is the original number of red tiles, and 50 is the new total.

questions.prompt: In a group of 120 students, 70 play chess, 50 play football, and 20 play both. If a student who plays chess is chosen at random, what is the probability that the student also plays football?
questions.explanation: Only the 70 chess players count, and 20 of them also play football: $\dfrac{20}{70} = \dfrac{2}{7}$. $\dfrac{2}{5}$ divides by the number of football players instead.

questions.prompt: A bag contains only red tiles and green tiles. If one tile is chosen at random, the probability that it is red is $\dfrac{3}{8}$. If the bag contains 15 green tiles, how many red tiles does it contain?
questions.explanation: Green tiles make up $1 - \dfrac{3}{8} = \dfrac{5}{8}$ of the bag, so the bag holds $15 \div \dfrac{5}{8} = 24$ tiles. Red tiles: $24 - 15 = 9$.

questions.prompt: A survey asked 250 workers in two cities whether they work remotely or on-site. The results are shown in the table. If one of the workers who work on-site is chosen at random, what is the probability that the worker is from Vancouver?
questions.explanation: Only the 180 on-site workers count, and 78 of them are from Vancouver: $\dfrac{78}{180} = \dfrac{13}{30}$.

questions.prompt: The table shows the results of a survey of 120 visitors to a textile museum, sorted by age group and by whether they attended a weaving workshop. If a visitor who attended a workshop is selected at random, what is the probability that the visitor is under 18 years old?
questions.explanation: Only the 45 visitors who attended a workshop count. Of these, 18 are under 18, and $\dfrac{18}{45} = \dfrac{2}{5}$.

questions.prompt: A box of robot parts contains 12 red connectors, 8 blue connectors, and 20 green connectors. If one connector is chosen at random from the box, what is the probability that it is blue?
questions.explanation: There are $12 + 8 + 20 = 40$ connectors, and 8 are blue: $\dfrac{8}{40} = \dfrac{1}{5}$.

questions.prompt: The table shows the results of a study of 80 sites near the front of a glacier, sorted by the direction each site faces and by whether the ice at the site was retreating or stable. If a site where the ice was stable is selected at random, what is the probability that the site faces north?
questions.explanation: Only the 29 stable sites count, and 22 of them face north: $\dfrac{22}{29}$. $\dfrac{11}{20}$ is the probability that a north-facing site is stable, which reverses the condition.

questions.prompt: The table shows the activity chosen by each of the 150 participants at a summer sports camp in Denver. If a participant who chose tennis is selected at random, what is the probability that the participant is 14 or older?
questions.explanation: Only the 38 tennis players count. Of these, 24 are 14 or older, and $\dfrac{24}{38} = \dfrac{12}{19}$.

questions.prompt: A box contains 6 green tokens, 9 yellow tokens, and 5 white tokens. If one token is chosen at random, what is the probability that it is yellow?
questions.explanation: There are $6 + 9 + 5 = 20$ tokens, and 9 of them are yellow.

questions.prompt: Of the 60 members of a games club, 36 play chess, 25 play go, and 10 play both games. If a member who plays at least one of the two games is selected at random, what is the probability that the member plays both games?
questions.explanation: Members who play at least one game: $36 + 25 - 10 = 51$. Of these, 10 play both, so the probability is $\dfrac{10}{51}$. Adding 36 and 25 without subtracting the overlap gives the wrong total of 61.

questions.prompt: A jar contains only red beads and white beads. There are 12 red beads, and the probability of choosing a red bead at random is $\dfrac{3}{8}$. How many white beads are in the jar?
questions.explanation: If $\dfrac{12}{T} = \dfrac{3}{8}$, the jar holds $T = 32$ beads in all, so there are $32 - 12 = 20$ white beads.

questions.prompt: The table shows the number of students in a school music club, by grade and by whether they play an instrument. If one student is chosen at random from the club, what is the probability that the student plays an instrument?
questions.explanation: $12 + 15 = 27$ of the 60 students play an instrument, and $\dfrac{27}{60} = \dfrac{9}{20}$.

questions.prompt: A survey asked 300 residents of a city how they prefer to travel to work. The results are shown in the table. If a resident who prefers the metro is chosen at random, what is the probability that the resident is under 30 years old?
questions.explanation: Only the 126 residents who prefer the metro count, and 72 of them are under 30: $\dfrac{72}{126} = \dfrac{4}{7}$. $\dfrac{3}{5}$ is the share of under-30 residents who prefer the metro, which reverses the condition.

questions.prompt: The table shows the results of a survey of 160 visitors to a dance festival in Edinburgh about which kind of performance they preferred. If a visitor who preferred folk dance is chosen at random, what is the probability that the visitor is a student?
questions.explanation: Only the 90 visitors who preferred folk dance count, and 38 of them are students: $\dfrac{38}{90} = \dfrac{19}{45}$. Dividing by 80 (all students) answers a different question.

questions.prompt: A jar contains 6 red candies, 9 yellow candies, and 5 green candies. If one candy is chosen at random, what is the probability that it is yellow?
questions.explanation: There are $6 + 9 + 5 = 20$ candies, and 9 are yellow, so the probability is $\dfrac{9}{20}$.

questions.prompt: The table summarizes a survey of 250 shoppers at a market who were asked whether they had used a discount coupon. If one of the shoppers who did not use a coupon is chosen at random, what is the probability that the shopper is a weekend shopper?
questions.explanation: Only the 160 shoppers who did not use a coupon count, and 76 of them shopped on a weekend: $\dfrac{76}{160} = \dfrac{19}{40}$. Dividing by 130 (all weekend shoppers) gives $\dfrac{38}{65}$, which answers a different question.

questions.prompt: The table shows the numbers of apricot trees and peach trees in two orchards. If a tree is chosen at random from the South orchard, what is the probability that it is a peach tree?
questions.explanation: Only the 60 trees in the South orchard count, and 32 of them are peach trees: $\dfrac{32}{60} = \dfrac{8}{15}$.

questions.prompt: The table shows how the residents surveyed in two districts of a city usually commute. If a resident who does not commute by car is chosen at random, what is the probability that the resident lives in the South district?
questions.explanation: Residents who do not commute by car: North has $36 + 16 = 52$ and South has $58 + 30 = 88$, for 140 in all. So the probability is $\dfrac{88}{140} = \dfrac{22}{35}$. Dividing by 150 or 250 uses the wrong group.

questions.prompt: A bag contains 5 red, 7 blue and 8 green marbles. Two marbles are taken out at random, one after the other, without replacement. What is the probability that both marbles are blue?
questions.explanation: The first marble is blue with probability $\dfrac{7}{20}$. Then 6 of the remaining 19 are blue, so the probability is $\dfrac{7}{20} \cdot \dfrac{6}{19} = \dfrac{42}{380} = \dfrac{21}{190}$. Choice B assumes the first marble is put back.

questions.prompt: A spinner is divided into 8 equal sections numbered 1 through 8. If the spinner is spun once, what is the probability that it lands on a number greater than 5?
questions.explanation: The numbers greater than 5 are 6, 7 and 8: 3 of the 8 equal sections. So the probability is $\dfrac{3}{8}$.

questions.prompt: The table shows the results of a survey of 200 students about whether they prefer online or in-person classes. If a student who prefers in-person classes is chosen at random, what is the probability that the student is a junior?
questions.explanation: Of the 102 students who prefer in-person classes, 36 are juniors, so the probability is $\dfrac{36}{102} = \dfrac{6}{17}$. Choice C divides by the 90 juniors instead, and choice D divides by all 200 students.

questions.prompt: In a class of 30 students, 12 have a dog, 8 have a cat, and 4 have both a dog and a cat. If a student is chosen at random from the class, what is the probability that the student has a dog or a cat?
questions.explanation: Students with a dog or a cat: $12 + 8 - 4 = 16$, since the 4 with both are counted twice. The probability is $\dfrac{16}{30} = \dfrac{8}{15}$. Choice A forgets to subtract the overlap.

questions.prompt: A box contains 4 red pens and 6 blue pens. If one pen is chosen at random, what is the probability that it is blue?
questions.explanation: 6 of the 10 pens are blue, so the probability is $\dfrac{6}{10} = \dfrac{3}{5}$. Choice A divides by the 4 red pens only.

questions.prompt: A clinic tested 200 people for an allergy. Of the 80 people who have the allergy, 60 tested positive. Of the 120 people who do not have the allergy, 18 tested positive. If a person who tested positive is chosen at random, what is the probability that the person has the allergy?
questions.explanation: In total, $60 + 18 = 78$ people tested positive, and 60 of them have the allergy, so the probability is $\dfrac{60}{78} = \dfrac{10}{13}$. Choice A is the probability of testing positive given the allergy.

questions.prompt: Each of 40 students chose either art or music as an elective. 15 chose art and 25 chose music. If one of the students is chosen at random, what is the probability that the student chose art?
questions.explanation: 15 of the 40 students chose art, so the probability is $\dfrac{15}{40} = \dfrac{3}{8}$.

questions.prompt: A fair six-sided die has faces numbered 1 through 6. If the die is rolled once, what is the probability of rolling an even number?
questions.explanation: The even numbers are 2, 4 and 6: 3 of the 6 faces. So the probability is $\dfrac{3}{6} = \dfrac{1}{2}$.

questions.prompt: In a group of 60 athletes, 24 play basketball, 30 play soccer, and 10 play both. If an athlete who plays soccer is chosen at random, what is the probability that the athlete also plays basketball?
questions.explanation: Of the 30 soccer players, 10 also play basketball, so the probability is $\dfrac{10}{30} = \dfrac{1}{3}$. Choice B divides by all 60 athletes, and choice C divides by the 24 basketball players.

questions.prompt: Two fair coins are tossed. What is the probability that both coins land heads up?
questions.explanation: There are 4 equally likely outcomes (HH, HT, TH, TT), and one of them is HH, so the probability is $\dfrac{1}{4}$.

questions.prompt: Twenty cards are numbered 1 through 20. If one card is chosen at random, what is the probability that its number is a multiple of 5?
questions.explanation: The multiples of 5 are 5, 10, 15 and 20: 4 of the 20 cards. The probability is $\dfrac{4}{20} = \dfrac{1}{5}$.

questions.prompt: The table shows how many 10th and 11th graders at a school joined the science club. If a student in the science club is chosen at random, what is the probability that the student is in 10th grade?
questions.explanation: There are 70 club members, and 30 of them are in 10th grade, so the probability is $\dfrac{30}{70} = \dfrac{3}{7}$. Choice A divides by the 75 tenth graders instead, and choice C divides by all 150 students.

questions.prompt: A bag contains 3 red, 5 green and 2 yellow marbles. If one marble is chosen at random, what is the probability that it is NOT green?
questions.explanation: 5 of the 10 marbles are not green (3 red and 2 yellow), so the probability is $\dfrac{5}{10} = \dfrac{1}{2}$.

questions.prompt: One letter is chosen at random from the word MATH. What is the probability that the letter is a vowel?
questions.explanation: Only A is a vowel, so 1 of the 4 letters is a vowel: $\dfrac{1}{4}$.

questions.prompt: The table shows how 200 customers paid at two stores. If a customer who paid with cash is chosen at random, what is the probability that the customer shopped at Store B?
questions.explanation: Of the 80 cash customers, 50 shopped at Store B, so the probability is $\dfrac{50}{80} = \dfrac{5}{8}$. Choice A divides by the 100 Store B customers instead.

questions.prompt: The table shows the number of students in grades 10 and 11 who belong to the chess club or the robotics club at a school. Each student belongs to exactly one of the two clubs. If a student is selected at random from the robotics club, what is the probability that the student is in grade 11?
questions.explanation: The robotics club has 28 students, and 10 of them are in grade 11: $\frac{10}{28} = \frac{5}{14}$. Choice B uses the 30 grade 11 students as the total instead.

questions.prompt: A bag contains 4 red marbles, 6 blue marbles, and 10 green marbles. If one marble is selected at random from the bag, what is the probability that the marble is NOT green?
questions.explanation: There are $4 + 6 = 10$ marbles that are not green, out of 20 in total: $\frac{10}{20} = \frac{1}{2}$.

questions.prompt: In a survey of 500 people, $60\%$ own a car. Of the car owners, $25\%$ also own a bicycle. Of the people who do not own a car, $70\%$ own a bicycle. If a person from the survey who owns a bicycle is selected at random, what is the probability that the person also owns a car?
questions.explanation: Car owners: 300, and $0.25 \times 300 = 75$ of them own bicycles. Non-owners: 200, and $0.70 \times 200 = 140$ of them own bicycles. Of the $215$ bicycle owners, 75 own cars: $\frac{75}{215} = \frac{15}{43}$. Choice B is the probability the other way around, P(bicycle given car).

questions.prompt: The frequency table summarizes the lengths of 23 eggs. If one of these eggs is selected at random, what is the probability of selecting an egg with a length of 39 millimeters?
questions.explanation: 6 of the 23 eggs are 39 mm long, so the probability is $\frac{6}{23}$. Choice C is the probability that the egg is *not* 39 mm.

questions.prompt: The table shows the distribution of the direction and speed of 65 moving objects. If one of these objects is selected at random and its speed is at most 30 meters per second, what is the probability that the object was moving in direction B?
questions.explanation: Only objects with speed at most 30 m/s count: $14 + 26 = 40$ of them. Of these, $8 + 11 = 19$ moved in direction B. The probability is $\frac{19}{40}$. C wrongly divides by all 65 objects.

questions.prompt: A bag contains $6$ red marbles, $9$ blue marbles, and $5$ green marbles. If one marble is chosen at random, what is the probability that it is blue?
questions.explanation: There are $6 + 9 + 5 = 20$ marbles, and $9$ are blue, so the probability is $\frac{9}{20}$.

questions.prompt:
A total of $50$ people attended a conference and were offered $4$ types of entrees. The table shows the number of people who chose each type of entree.

If one of these people is selected at random, what is the probability of selecting a person who chose a vegetarian entree?
questions.explanation: $9$ of the $50$ people chose vegetarian, so the probability is $\frac{9}{50}$.

questions.prompt: In a survey of $200$ students, $120$ said they play a sport, $80$ said they play a musical instrument, and $50$ said they do both. If one of the students who play a sport is chosen at random, what is the probability that this student also plays a musical instrument?
questions.explanation: Only the $120$ sport players are considered. Of them, $50$ also play an instrument, so the probability is $\frac{50}{120} = \frac{5}{12}$. Choice A uses all $200$ students.

questions.prompt: The table shows the $40$ members of a school music club, by grade and by whether they play an instrument. If a member who plays an instrument is selected at random, what is the probability that the member is in grade $11$?
questions.explanation: $8 + 12 = 20$ members play an instrument, and $12$ of them are in grade $11$: $\frac{12}{20} = \frac{3}{5}$.

questions.prompt: A box contains $5$ red pencils, $9$ blue pencils, and $6$ black pencils. If one pencil is selected at random, what is the probability that it is black?
questions.explanation: There are $5 + 9 + 6 = 20$ pencils and $6$ are black: $\frac{6}{20} = \frac{3}{10}$.

questions.prompt: In a survey of $250$ people, $140$ said they own a dog, $90$ said they own a cat, and $45$ said they own both a dog and a cat. If one of the people who own a cat is selected at random, what is the probability that this person also owns a dog?
questions.explanation: Among the $90$ cat owners, $45$ also own a dog: $\frac{45}{90} = \frac{1}{2}$. ($\frac{9}{28} = \frac{45}{140}$ answers the reverse question.)

questions.prompt: Each of the $50$ people at a conference chose one of $4$ types of entrees, as shown in the table. If one of these $50$ people is selected at random, what is the probability that the person chose a vegetarian entree?
questions.explanation: $7$ of the $50$ people chose vegetarian, so the probability is $\frac{7}{50}$.

questions.prompt: A spinner is divided into $10$ equal sections numbered $1$ through $10$. If the spinner is spun once, what is the probability that it lands on an even number greater than $4$?
questions.explanation: The even numbers greater than $4$ are $6$, $8$, and $10$: $3$ of the $10$ sections.
